ref_atoms.ref_content: This recoverable alert is triggered upon detecting an update error in the shadowed Control Register. The content of the Control Register is not modified (See Control Register). The AES unit can be recovered from such a condition by restarting the AES operation, i.e., by re-writing the Control Register. This should be monitored by the system.

ref_atoms.ref_content: This fatal alert is triggered upon detecting a fatal fault inside the AES unit. Examples for such faults include i) storage errors in the shadowed Control Register, ii) any internal FSM entering an invalid state, iii) any sparsely encoded signal taking on an invalid value, iv) errors in the internal round counter, v) escalations triggered by the life cycle controller, and vi) fatal integrity failures on the TL-UL bus. The AES unit cannot recover from such an error and needs to be reset.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Lists explicit fault sources (storage errors, FSM invalid state, sparse encoding violation, round counter error, lifecycle escalation, bus integrity) and states the unrecoverable nature requiring reset, giving clear verification targets.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Initial Key Registers Share 0. The actual initial key corresponds to Initial Key Registers Share 0 XORed with Initial Key Registers Share 1. Loaded into the internal Full Key register upon starting encryption/decryption of the next block. All key registers (Share 0 and Share 1) must be written at least once when the key is changed, regardless of key length (write random data for unused bits). The order in which the registers are updated does not matter. Can only be updated when the AES unit is idle. If the AES unit is non-idle, writes to these registers are ignored. Upon reset, these registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Detailed behavior: key shares XOR to form full key, load timing, write requirements, idle‑only update restriction, write ignore during busy, and pseudo‑random clear on reset. All are concrete hardware rules.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Initial Key Registers Share 1. The actual initial key corresponds to Initial Key Registers Share 0 XORed with Initial Key Registers Share 1. Loaded into the internal Full Key register upon starting encryption/decryption of the next block. All key registers (Share 0 and Share 1) must be written at least once when the key is changed, regardless of key length (write random data for unused bits). The order in which the registers are updated does not matter. Can only be updated when the AES unit is idle. If the AES unit is non-idle, writes to these registers are ignored. Upon reset, these registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Same concrete behaviors as KEY_SHARE0: XOR key construction, load triggering, write‑all requirement, idle‑only write, busy write ignore, and pseudo‑random reset clear.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Initialization Vector Registers. The initialization vector (IV) or initial counter value must be written to these registers when starting a new message in CBC or CTR mode, respectively. In CBC and CTR modes, the AES unit does not start encryption/decryption with a partially updated IV. Each register has to be written at least once. The order in which the registers are written does not matter. If the AES unit is non-idle, writes to these registers are ignored. Whenever starting a new message, the corresponding IV value must be provided by the processor. Once started, the AES unit automatically updates the contents of these registers. In ECB mode, the IV registers are not used and do not need to be configured. Upon reset, these registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Precise IV usage rules per mode, atomic write requirement, idle‑only write, automatic hardware update behavior, and pseudo‑random reset clearing, all giving clear verification conditions.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Input Data Registers. If MANUAL_OPERATION=0, the AES unit automatically starts encryption/decryption after all Input Data registers have been written. Each register has to be written at least once. The order in which the registers are written does not matter. Loaded into the internal State register upon starting encryption/decryption of the next block. After that, the processor can update the Input Data registers (See INPUT_READY field of Status Register). Upon reset, these registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Defines auto‑start condition for data input, write‑all requirement, transfer to internal state, readiness indication via INPUT_READY, and pseudo‑random reset clearing – all specific hardware behaviors.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Output Data Register. Holds the output data produced by the AES unit during the last encryption/decryption operation. If MANUAL_OPERATION=0, the AES unit is stalled when the previous output data has not yet been read and is about to be overwritten. Each register has to be read at least once. The order in which the registers are read does not matter. Upon reset, these registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes stall behavior in automatic mode to prevent data loss, read‑all requirement, and pseudo‑random reset clearing, providing explicit verification scenarios.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Control Register. Can only be updated when the AES unit is idle. If the AES unit is non-idle, writes to this register are ignored. This register is shadowed, meaning two subsequent write operations are required to change its content. If the two write operations try to set a different value, a recoverable alert is triggered. A read operation clears the internal phase tracking: The next write operation is always considered a first write operation of an update sequence. Any write operation to this register will clear the status tracking required for automatic mode. A write to the Control Register is considered the start of a new message. Hence, software needs to provide new key, IV and input data afterwards. Fields: OPERATION (bits 1:0): 2-bit one-hot field to select the operation of AES unit. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set and value 2'b00, are mapped to AES_ENC (2'b01). MODE (bits 7:2): 6-bit one-hot field to select AES block cipher mode. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set and value 6'b00_0000, are mapped to AES_NONE (6'b10_0000). KEY_LEN (bits 10:8): 3-bit one-hot field to select AES key length. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set, value 3'b000, and value 3'b010 in case 192-bit keys are not supported (because disabled at compile time) are mapped to AES_256 (3'b100). SIDELOAD (bit 11): Controls whether the AES unit uses the key provided by the key manager via key sideload interface (1) or the key provided by software via Initial Key Registers. PRNG_RESEED_RATE (bits 14:12): 3-bit one-hot field to control the reseeding rate of the internal PRNG used for masking. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set and value 3'b000 are mapped to the highest reseeding rate PER_1 (3'b001). MANUAL_OPERATION (bit 15): Controls whether the AES unit is operated in normal/automatic mode (0) or fully manual mode (1). In automatic mode, the AES unit automatically starts to encrypt/decrypt when it receives new input data, and stalls during the last encryption/decryption cycle if the previous output data has not yet been read. Note that the corresponding status tracking is automatically cleared upon a write to the Control Register. In manual mode, the AES unit only starts to encrypt/decrypt after receiving a start trigger, and overwrites previous output data irrespective of whether it has been read out or not.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Comprehensive register behavior: idle‑only write, shadow update with two‑phase commit and alert on mismatch, read resets update phase, write clears auto‑mode tracking and starts new message. Each field has concrete definitions including invalid value mappings and operational modes with precise automation/stall rules.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Auxiliary Control Register. This register is shadowed, meaning two subsequent write operations are required to change its content. If the two write operations try to set a different value, a recoverable alert is triggered. A read operation clears the internal phase tracking: The next write operation is always considered a first write operation of an update sequence. Fields: KEY_TOUCH_FORCES_RESEED (bit 0): Controls whether providing a new key triggers the reseeding of internal pseudo-random number generators used for clearing and masking (1) or not (0). FORCE_MASKS (bit 1): Allow the internal masking PRNG to advance (0) or force its internal state (1) leading to constant masks. Setting all masks to constant value can be useful when performing SCA. To completely disable the masking, the second key share must be zero as well. In addition, a special seed needs to be loaded into the masking PRNG using the EDN interface. Only applicable if both the Masking parameter and the SecAllowForcingMasks parameter are set to one.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Shadowed register with two‑phase update and error alert; fields define concrete hardware controls for reseed‑on‑key‑touch and mask forcing with explicit dependency on compile‑time parameters and EDN seed loading.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Lock bit for Auxiliary Control Register. If the Auxiliary Control Register configuration enable bit is cleared to 0, the Auxiliary Control Register cannot be written anymore.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes a write‑once lock mechanism for the Auxiliary Control Register, a simple but precise hardware behavior to verify.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Trigger Register. Each bit is individually cleared to zero when executing the corresponding trigger. While executing any of the triggered operations, the AES unit will set the IDLE bit in the Status Register to zero. The processor must check the Status Register before triggering further actions. For example, writes to Initial Key and IV Registers are ignored while the AES unit is busy. Writes to the Input Data Registers are not ignored but the data will be cleared if a KEY_IV_DATA_IN_CLEAR operation is pending. Fields: START (bit 0): Keep AES unit paused (0) or trigger the encryption/decryption of one data block (1). This trigger is cleared to 0 if MANUAL_OPERATION=0 or if MODE=AES_NONE. KEY_IV_DATA_IN_CLEAR (bit 1): Keep current values in Initial Key, internal Full Key and Decryption Key registers, IV registers and Input Data registers (0) or clear all those registers with pseudo-random data (1). DATA_OUT_CLEAR (bit 2): Keep current values in Output Data registers (0) or clear those registers with pseudo-random data (1). PRNG_RESEED (bit 3): Keep continuing with the current states of the internal pseudo-random number generators used for register clearing and masking (0) or perform a reseed of the internal states from the connected entropy source (1). If the KEY_TOUCH_FORCES_RESEED bit in the Auxiliary Control Register is set to one, this trigger will automatically get set after providing a new initial key.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Defines trigger semantics: self‑clearing bits, IDLE assertion, interaction with busy state, ignore vs clear of writes, and field‑specific behaviors including forced clearing in certain modes and automatic reseed trigger on key change.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Status Register. Fields: IDLE (bit 0): The AES unit is idle (1) or busy (0). This flag is 0 if one of the following operations is currently running: i) encryption/decryption, ii) register clearing or iii) PRNG reseeding. This flag is also 0 if an encryption/decryption is running but the AES unit is stalled. STALL (bit 1): The AES unit is not stalled (0) or stalled (1) because there is previous output data that must be read by the processor before the AES unit can overwrite this data. This flag is not meaningful if MANUAL_OPERATION=1. OUTPUT_LOST (bit 2): All previous output data has been fully read by the processor (0) or at least one previous output data block has been lost (1). It has been overwritten by the AES unit before the processor could fully read it. Once set to 1, this flag remains set until AES operation is restarted by re-writing the Control Register. The primary use of this flag is for design verification. This flag is not meaningful if MANUAL_OPERATION=0. OUTPUT_VALID (bit 3): The AES unit has no valid output (0) or has valid output data (1). INPUT_READY (bit 4): The AES unit is ready (1) or not ready (0) to receive new data input via the DATA_IN registers. If the present values in the DATA_IN registers have not yet been loaded into the module this flag is 0 (not ready). ALERT_RECOV_CTRL_UPDATE_ERR (bit 5): An update error has not occurred (0) or has occurred (1) in the shadowed Control Register. AES operation needs to be restarted by re-writing the Control Register. ALERT_FATAL_FAULT (bit 6): No fatal fault has occurred inside the AES unit (0). A fatal fault has occurred and the AES unit needs to be reset (1). Examples for fatal faults include i) storage errors in the Control Register, ii) if any internal FSM enters an invalid state, iii) if any sparsely encoded signal takes on an invalid value, iv) errors in the internal round counter, v) escalations triggered by the life cycle controller, and vi) fatal integrity failures on the TL-UL bus.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Each status bit defines precise conditions for set/clear, dependencies on mode (MANUAL_OPERATION), clearing events, and link to alerts and fault sources. Provides numerous checkable hardware state assertions.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Covers that all valid settings for operation (encode/decode/illegal), mode (all modes + illegal/aes_none), key_len (128/192/256 + illegal), sideload, prng_reseed_rate (all + illegal), and manual operation have been tested, including illegal values. All valid combinations of these will be crossed.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Exhaustively tests control register fields and their combinations, covering both valid and illegal values, ensuring hardware reacts correctly.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Covers that when key_touch_forces_reseed is enabled, a complete write of the key forces a reseed (DUT goes out of idle after a full key is provided), and that when key_touch_forces_reseed = 0, this does not happen.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Verifies the key_touch_forces_reseed control bit behavior: forcing reseed after key write and returning to idle, specifying exact condition.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Covers that start initiates an operation in manual mode but not when not in manual mode. A write to key_iv_data_in/data_out_clear clears the data from the register. Additionally, transitioning from automatic to manual mode prevents triggering a start without re-configuring (writing to CTRL).
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Verifies start trigger behavior per mode, clear functionality of data registers, and mode transition requiring CTRL reconfiguration, pinpointing specific control paths.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Cover that a recoverable error has been seen when the DUT is idle but just about to start, and when the DUT is busy.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Ensures fault injection triggers recoverable error in both idle-just-before-start and busy states, targeting error reporting timing.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Cover that the DUT self clearing is working correctly. After reset, manually writing trigger.start and polling status.idle must show DUT stays idle; output registers should contain random data (output cleared).
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes self-clearing mechanism: reset disallows start, output registers cleared with random data, naming trigger.start and status.idle signals.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Cover that a busy DUT cannot be manipulated: trying to change the configuration (CTRL), key, or IV while busy should be prevented.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Verifies busy-lock mechanism for CTRL, key, and IV registers, preventing configuration changes during operation.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Cover sideload functionality: an operation does not start before a valid key is present at the sideload interface when sideload is enabled; a key on the sideload interface is not consumed when sideload is disabled.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Validates sideload handshake: operation waits for valid key in enabled mode; key ignored when disabled, referencing valid signal.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The AES unit supports both encryption and decryption for AES-128/192/256 in ECB, CBC, CFB, OFB and CTR modes using a single, shared data path. That is, it can either do encryption or decryption but not both at the same time.

When the key is changed before ECB/CBC decryption, there is an initial delay while the key expanding mechanism iteratively computes the start key for decryption. The duration equals the latency for encrypting one 16B block: 12/14/16 cycles for AES-128/192/256. Once computed, the start key is stored and switching between encryption/decryption occurs without overhead. For encryption or CFB, OFB, CTR modes, there is no such delay upon key change.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: 具体描述了密钥变更后ECB/CBC解密的初始延迟周期数（12/14/16周期）以及加密和其他模式无延迟的行为。

ref_atoms.ref_content: In automatic mode (MANUAL_OPERATION=0 in CTRL_SHADOWED), the AES unit automatically starts encryption/decryption when the previous operation finished, new input data is available, all input registers written at least once (any order), and in CBC/CFB/OFB/CTR modes the IV is ready (all IV registers written at least once or none since last update; partially updated IV will not start). In manual mode (MANUAL_OPERATION=1), encryption/decryption starts only when the START bit in TRIGGER is set to 1, and START is automatically cleared to 0 once the next operation starts.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: 明确的具体寄存器（CTRL_SHADOWED.MANUAL_OPERATION, TRIGGER.START）和启动条件（输入/IV就绪条件），可验证。

ref_atoms.ref_content: The AES unit indicates output data availability via a status register. A back-pressure mechanism stalls the AES unit when finishing a block but previous output data not yet read by the processor; it hangs, does not drop data, and continues only after the previous output registers are read (any order, each read at least once). In manual mode (MANUAL_OPERATION=1 in CTRL_SHADOWED), the AES unit never stalls and overwrites previous output data regardless of read status.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: 描述输出背压机制，涉及状态寄存器、输出寄存器和MANUAL_OPERATION位的具体行为，可验证挂起和覆盖条件。

ref_atoms.ref_content: In the final round, the internal State register is cleared with pseudo-random data, and the output is forwarded to the output register but not stored back into the State register. Depending on the cipher mode, the output may be XORed with the IV registers (CBC decryption) or previous input data (CFB, OFB, CTR modes).
ref_atoms.kind_reason: 详细描述了最后轮中状态寄存器清除伪随机数据的行为，以及输出与IV/前输入数据的XOR逻辑，针对特定模式和寄存器。

ref_atoms.ref_content: The processor can only update the IV registers when the AES unit is idle. In CBC or CTR mode, when the AES unit is busy, it updates the IV registers itself. The IV registers are updated with output data (CBC encryption) or previous input data (CBC decryption); in CFB mode with output data; in OFB mode with the output of the final cipher round before XORing with previous input data.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: 明确IV寄存器的更新权限（处理器仅空闲时更新，AES单元在忙碌时自我更新）以及不同模式下的更新数据源，可验证。

ref_atoms.ref_content: When the SIDELOAD bit in CTRL_SHADOWED is set to 1, any processor writes to the Initial Key registers (KEY_SHARE0_0 - KEY_SHARE1_7) are ignored. The AES unit only starts encryption/decryption if the sideload key is marked as valid (via key manager valid signal). To use a sideload key, the processor must wait for idle, wait for the key manager to assert valid, then write to CTRL_SHADOWED to start a new message.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: 描述了旁路密钥模式下处理器写入被忽略和有效信号要求的具体寄存器（CTRL_SHADOWED.SIDELOAD, KEY_SHARE*寄存器），有明确行为。

ref_atoms.ref_content: The DOM S-Box has a latency of 5 clock cycles. All other S-Box implementations (Masked Canright, unmasked Canright, LUT) are fully combinational with one S-Box evaluation per clock cycle.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: 具体描述了DOM S-Box的5周期延迟和其他实现每周期评估的行为，针对S-Box模块。

ref_atoms.ref_content: The masking PRNG is automatically reseeded with fresh entropy from EDN 1) whenever a new key is provided (if CTRL_AUX_SHADOWED.KEY_TOUCH_FORCES_RESEED is enabled) and 2) based on a block counter configured via CTRL_SHADOWED.PRNG_RESEED_RATE. Software can also manually initiate a reseed via TRIGGER.PRNG_RESEED.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: 明确PRNG重播种的自动条件和配置寄存器（CTRL_AUX_SHADOWED.KEY_TOUCH_FORCES_RESEED, CTRL_SHADOWED.PRNG_RESEED_RATE, TRIGGER.PRNG_RESEED），可验证。

ref_atoms.ref_content: The main control register (CTRL_SHADOWED) is shadowed: software performs two write operations to update, and a shadow copy is constantly compared with the actual register. If a mismatch occurs, a fatal alert is triggered.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: 描述影子寄存器的更新机制和比较检测，涉及CTRL_SHADOWED和fatal alert。

ref_atoms.ref_content: If any countermeasure (shadow register mismatch, sparse encoding fault, multi-rail control logic fault, hardened round counter fault) detects a fault, a fatal alert is triggered. Internal FSMs go to a terminal error state, the AES unit ceases to release data and locks up until a system reset. This condition is reported in STATUS.ALERT_FATAL_FAULT.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: 具体描述了故障检测后的致命警报、终端错误状态和锁定行为，涉及STATUS.ALERT_FATAL_FAULT寄存器位。

ref_atoms.ref_content: Upon reset or if initiated by software, all major key and data registers inside the AES module are cleared with pseudo-random data. The state registers inside the cipher core are also cleared with PRD during the last round of every encryption/decryption.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: 明确了寄存器清除伪随机数据的条件和范围，包括复位/软件触发和每轮最后的状态清除。

ref_atoms.ref_content: The initial key and control register can only be updated by the processor when the AES unit is idle.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: 明确处理器更新初始密钥和控制寄存器的空闲条件，可验证。

ref_atoms.ref_content: In CTR mode, the counter module iteratively increments the 128-bit counter value stored in the IV register using a 16-bit counter, requiring 8 clock cycles per increment. The counter value is used in the first round only, so the overall throughput is not affected given the 12/14/16-cycle block latency.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: 描述CTR模式下计数器增量所需周期数（8个周期）和用法，可验证。

ref_atoms.ref_content: While the AES unit is performing encryption/decryption, the processor can safely write the next input data block into the CSRs or read the previous output data block from the CSRs. The internal State register is not exposed via the bus interface.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: 描述流水线操作：处理期间可预写入下一输入和回读上一输出，保护内部状态，可验证。
